cs.t: Isn't this a chicken and egg problem? Why would OS vendors spend time implementing this on their side if the drives don't support it? The difference here being that it's not clear to me that there's much cost on the drive side to actually allow this. Aside maybe for the will to segment the market. To me, this looks like the whole sector size situation. OSs, including regular Windows, have supported 4K drives for quite a while now. I bought a Samsung 980 (non-pro) the other day that still pretends to have 512B sectors. The OEM drive in my laptop (some kind of Samsung) can be formatted with a 4k namespace, but the default is also 512B. The 980 doesn't even support this.
cs.th: I tested four NVMe SSDs from four vendors – half lose FLUSH’d data on power loss
